text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- President Ion Iliescu denied there was a diesel oil shortage, saying it was caused by distribution malfunctions.
- Three weeks after its offical opening, Romania's over-the-counter market has not struck a single deal yet, due to complicated registring procedures.
- Some 30 of 4,000 companies involved in mass privatisation and the OTC market have become members of the shareholders registrar.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romania is confronted with an acute diesel oil shortage, with all local supplies being channelled to the harvest.

- Fiscal regulations allowing Romanian companies to spend only three percent of their gross annual income on advertising undermine their promotion. Managers demand the percentage be increased to 10 or 15 percent.
- The World Bank has granted 6.0 million ECU for environment projects.
- Brasov-based plane maker IAR Ghimbav is discussing the sale of about 30 two-seater planes per year to U.S. companies.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The leu rate rose to over 4,000 to the dollar at exchange shops.
- Diesel oil shortages in agriculture have pushed up food prices, especially of eggs and cheese.
- State companies owe more than 1,000 billion lei to the state insurance budget.
BURSA
- The newspaper says the dollar can be bought for 5,000 lei on the black market.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Romanian women buy an annual 50 million pairs of tights, 70 percent of which are locally-made.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Cigarette firm Davidoff wants to buy or build a factory in Romania and manufacture its brand with local tobacco.
LIBERTATEA
- Prices in Bucharest rose to up to $20,000 for a two-room appartment.
- The European Union extended 160,000 ECU to develop "agro-tourism" -- rural residents renting out their homes -- in four areas.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- An opinion poll conducted by a marketing institute shows the opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) leading with 35.6 percent of support in next months's general election, followed by the Social Democratic Union (USD) with 25.3 percent. The Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) of President Ion Iliescu trails in third place with 23.7 percent.
ADEVARUL

- An opinion poll by the IMAS institute puts incumbent Ion Iliescu ahead in the presdidential election, with 32 percent and ahead of CDR challenger Emil Constantinescu with 27 percent. A poll for the general election credits the CDR with 31 percent support and the PDSR with the 28.5.
- Police will watch over 43 regional electoral bureaus and 11,234 polling stations in 2,948 towns and villages.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The newspasper says in an editorial that the large number of presidential candidates can only benefit Iliescu.
- Some of the main presidential candidates' wives told state radio they will have no involvement in their husbands' activities if they are elected.
- The newspaper presents in a full-page report on the human side of Ioan Pop de Popa, presidential candidate of National Centre Union (UNC).
JURNALUL NATIONAL

- Gheorghe Funar, presidential candidate of the National Unity Party (PUNR), says leaders of the ruling PDSR and presidential advisers took large sums of money from the Caritas pyramid scheme before it collapsed, sucking in $1.0 billion worth of savings from four million Romanian investors.
COTIDIANUL
- The presidential campaign of reformist former Prime Minister Petre Roman is costing 280 million lei, said Traian Baseascu, vice-president of Roman's Democratic Party (PD).
DIMINEATA
- Gheorghe Pascu, financial expert of President Iliescu's campaign staff estimates that more than 2.5 billion lei will be spent in Iliescu's campaign. ($=3,306 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
